title: Meyer Davis and Lester Lanin approach him
summary: Society leaders Meyer Davis and Lester Lanin recruited Moore from the Metropole; Lanin took him to dinner.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, I was at the Metropole, Meyer Davis came in at one time, he invited me to his table and he asked me to have a drink with him. So I did, had a drink, and he says to me, 'We'd like to have you come and join the band. Why don't you come to the office, he's my card, come over and talk to me, I'd like to have you come with us.' I said, sure. That's the first time I ever met Meyer Davis, so the next day I didn't go to see Meyer Davis but I thought about
one of the great society band leaders.

the possibility, you know, so I didn't go and the next few days another band leader came in, society band leader, came to me and says to me, he ran in just at intermission time -- he said, "How long is that intermission?" I said it was 45 minutes. He said, "Get your horn, get your horn. Come with me over to --" I said, "Wait a minute, wait a minute, what's your name?" "You don't know me? I'm Lester Lanin." "Oh, glad to know you, Lester," I said, "I've heard so much about you, you're one of the great band leaders." He said, "Get your horn, get your horn. We've got a cab waiting." So we got in the cab and went over to the Astor Hotel across in Times Square and up in the ballroom, he had his group playing there, 12 pieces, so I didn't have too much time to be up there. So we played "The Saints Come Marching In." By that time I had to go back to the Metropole because my intermission was up. So that was my formal introduction to Lester Lanin and "Come and talk to me at the office, have dinner with me," I said, "Oh, sure, I'll go for the dinner." (Laughter) Anyway I went back to the Metropole, finished the night out, next two or three days I went over to see Lester. "You promised me dinner," because anytime they ask me for something to eat, I'm going to respond. So he took

me over to get me a nice T-bone steak. Well, anyway he said something about, the bass coming in that he wanted to use me and I said, 'Sure, all right, okay.' That's the way I started with Lester Lanin. Now, my entire field is different. I've gotten away from jazz for a while and I'm doing commercial tunes now with the dance music and it was a wonderful experience also to learn the society music and society pop style.

I think so. I've got enough memories to think about what happened in those years. You keep track of the years, I know that you're aware of what years that would be in. So at this point I've been with Lester Lanin for about 35 years.
Outside of the fact that we have another chapter coming on out of two years that I left to go with Armstrong again. This time it's not the big band, I joined the All Stars.
